answer: Picture an agent economy where each new identity must be vouched for by three incumbents picked by a random walk across a slowly rewiring trust graph. A lone honest agent finds a haven easily; a farm cannot, because the walk keeps landing inside clusters it must already own, and every fabricated edge raises the next identity's required reach. Cost grows superlinearly, like hauling rock through shale: the thousandth fake identity drags a thousand times more verified weight. Rewards accrue per distinct edge, not per node, so one opal of real standing outshines a heap of empty shells.
